statement: The program is a complete natlang package: `natlang check --json` on it reports no errors.

It has two or three input instances, each written as literal data, each with an exact checker (oracle exact or normalized against `expected`, or a trusted verifier under training/semantic_fp_tasks/verifiers/).
Each instance has a reference: a root eval script that runs the program's own helpers with scripted answers for its judgment calls, and the value it returns is accepted by the checker.
Each instance has at least three wrong answers of the right type, each from a named real mistake, and the checker rejects every one.
A strong teacher model running the root function on the instance with the real runtime returns an answer the checker accepts on at least one instance (a disagreement is adjudicated).
The program has at least three distinct judgments of meaning: `.nl` functions (or inline `nl` calls) with different instructions and typed results.
The answer depends on every judgment: for each judgment, the reference replayed with that judgment's scripted answers replaced by its trap reading returns an answer the checker rejects.
Each instance has a keyword baseline (a root script with no natural-language call that answers from surface cues), it runs to an answer, and the checker rejects it.

Every judgment is one narrow question of meaning with exactly one defensible answer on each item of the instances, every free text from outside that a judgment reads (documents, notes, descriptions, messages) is typed `Untrusted<...>` (identifiers, numbers and closed labels need not be), and each judgment receives the data it needs and nothing it must not see.
The call graph has at least five functions (`.nl` files and exported TypeScript helpers) and a call chain at least three deep (root, helper, judgment).
Each instance holds at least eight items, or at least 1,200 words of input text.

At least one judgment reads the result of another judgment, or of an exact stage computed from judgments, and at least two rules or stages interact so that their order or precedence decides the outcome.
The callable folder holds TypeScript with at least 40 non-blank lines of exact logic (parsing, ordering, aggregation, state transitions, graph walks) that the root's answer depends on.

The program uses at least three semantic-FP constructs: decide/readout decision, a @natlang/std collection or convergence combinator, a judgment passed, returned or partially applied, iterateOn with until, structural recursion, ensures, Is/Untrusted refinements, Neuralese<T>, a folder transaction, pluggable.

Every exact step (arithmetic, counting, sorting, parsing, record assembly, state updates) is TypeScript; `.nl` instructions state judgments of meaning and name the helpers they call, with no algorithm written out in prose.
The root returns a named type from types.ts whose fields carry doc comments; the output format is declared in types, not described in an instruction paragraph.

The idea differs from every atlas entry and every accepted idea in at least two of: user and job, core judgments, computational shape, input kind (`isNew`, by a model of another family than the inventor).
The submission contains no generator: instances are literal JSON written for this program, at most three, and no script in the submission produces inputs or answers.
